titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§275–277: Batu's feast, Güjüg and Qarγasun, and Ögödei's rebuke
part: §§275–277 — Batu's feast, Güjüg and Qarγasun, and Ögödei's rebuke
about: After the Kibchak campaign Batu sends word to Ögödei that Büri and Güjüg took offence at a feast, rode off in anger and called him and his followers old women. Ögödei, furious, curses Güjüg and Qarγasun and wants them sent to Batu for judgment; the officers plead that a steppe quarrel belongs on the steppe, Ögödei calms, and rebukes Güjüg for how he marched and boasted. He sends Güjüg and Qarγasun to Batu, and Büri to Cha'adai.

sentences.t: Batu Kibčaγčin ajan deġerēče Ögödei Qaγan-(n)a elčin-eče öčižü irerün:
sentences.l: Batu, Kibčaγčin campaign from-above, Ögödei Qaγan-to envoy-by reporting, coming:
sentences.i: Batu, on the Kibchak campaign, reported to Ögödei Qahan by an envoy, who came saying:
sentences.n: Deġerēče (Ming 上處 “from above”) is the awkward word: I read Kibčaγčin ajan deġerēče as “from the Kibchak campaign above/away” and take the envoy (elčin-eče, “by envoy”) as the one who “came”. Kibčaγčin is the Kipchaks, with an ending -čin I cannot explain. Qaγan-(n)a: the Ming 行 marks “to” the Qahan. Everything that follows to the closing mark at medetügei is the message Batu sent.

sentences.t: "Müṅke teṅgeri-jin küčün-dür qaγan abaγa-jin su-dur Meged balaγasun ebdežü Orusud irgen-i daγ̇uližu
sentences.l: "Müṅke teṅgeri-jin küčün-dür qaγan abaγa-jin su-dur Meged balaγasun ebdežü Orusud irgen-i daγ̇uližu
sentences.i: “By the strength of Eternal Heaven and by the fortune of the Qahan, my uncle, we broke the town of Meged and took the Orusud people captive,
sentences.n: Two dative-locatives, küčün-dür and su-dur, are “by strength” and “by fortune” (Ming 氣力裏, 福蔭裏). Qaγan abaγa-jin is “of the uncle Qahan” (Ming 叔叔的): Ögödei is Batu's uncle. Ebdežü and daγ̇uližu are two converbs in a chain, “breaking … plundering”; daγ̇uli- is uncertain (Ming 擄 “take captive”). Meged is a town (Ming 城名). The opening mark is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: harban nigen qarin irgen-i žüg-tür oroγ̇ulžu
sentences.l: ten one nations people-(obj) right-direction making-enter,
sentences.i: and we brought the people of eleven nations in, each in its proper way,
sentences.n: Harban nigen is “ten-one”, eleven. Qarin I take as “nation” from the Ming 邦 (tentative; elsewhere it is “back, again” or “division”). Žüg-tür (Ming 正行 “in the right direction”) is “in the proper way”. Oroγ̇ulžu = oro- “enter” + causative -γ̇ul- + converb -žu: “making them enter”, bringing them to submission.

sentences.t: altan žiluγ̇a ičun tatažu salulčaqui
sentences.l: Gold breast-strap withdrawing pulling parting
sentences.i: Drawing back the gold breast-strap (?), for the parting
sentences.n: Hard, and left tentative: altan žiluγ̇a is “gold bridle-strap” (Ming 金牽胷, a breast-strap or martingale), ičun (Ming 退) “withdrawing”, tatažu (Ming 扯着) “pulling”, salulčaqui (Ming 分離的) “of parting”. I take it as a ceremonial moment of taking leave before the feast; the exact image is not certain.

sentences.l: feast let-us-hold saying-together, great tent raising, feast-holding-at
sentences.i: we agreed together to hold a feast, and raised a great tent; at the holding of the feast

sentences.t: bi ede bükün köġüd-ün aqaqan boluγsan bolžu nigen qojar ajaγa ötög urida uγ̇uba keġen na-dur Büri, Güjüg, qojar maγ̇uilažu qurim ülü qurimlan morilaγdaba.
sentences.l: I these being sons-of elder having-become becoming, one two cup first toast drank saying me-to; Büri Güjüg two being-vexed feast not feasting were-mounted.
sentences.i: I, being the elder among these princes who were there, drank first, a cup or two of the toast, saying so. At me Büri and Güjüg, the two of them, took offence; refusing to feast, they were put on their horses.
sentences.n: Köġüd-ün aqaqan boluγsan: “having become the elder of the sons” (aqa + -qan, Ming 長些 “somewhat elder”, the -qan uncertain). Ötög is the toast (Ming 喝蓋/進酒). Na-dur is “to me” (Ming 我行), the person they were vexed at. Maγ̇uilažu is “being vexed” (Ming 煩惱着). Qurimlan morilaγdaba: the passive of morin “horse” + -la-, “were mounted” (Ming 被上馬子); I take it that they left in anger, and make the English “put on their horses”. Batu speaks throughout.

sentences.t: Batu sača böġed bolžu urida ker uγ̇uqun büleġe.
sentences.l: Batu equal being becoming, first how drinking was.
sentences.i: ‘Batu is only our equal: how was it that he drank first?’
sentences.n: Sača (Ming 齊等 “equal, on a par”) is the glossary's “alike”, here “equal”; böġed is the particle of sequence; uγ̇uqun is the stem uγ̇u- “drink” with an ending I cannot name. Ker büleġe: “how was it?”. The sense is Büri's complaint at Batu drinking the first toast.

sentences.t: Saqaltan emeged sačaγ̇un bolžu ösügei-jer tuližu ölmi-(i)jer gečikileküi keġežüġü.
sentences.l: Beard-having old-women equally becoming heel-by covering instep-by treading said.
sentences.i: ‘The bearded old women are all alike; (let us) cover (them) with the heel and trample (them) with the instep,’ he said.
sentences.n: Saqaltan emeged is “bearded old women” (Ming 髯有的婆婆每), an insult; I think it is aimed at Batu and those with him, but the Ming does not say so. Ösügei-jer ... ölmi-(i)jer are “with the heel … with the instep” (Ming 敎腳後根, 敎腳面), -jer read as an instrumental, which is not certain. Tuližu, “covering” (Ming 葢), is only a guess; gečikileküi (Ming 踐踏) is “trampling”.

sentences.t: Ba bürün busu heligetü bulγa irgen-dür morilaγ̇uldažu žöbi tabi bolqu bolba. keġežü
sentences.l: We being other liver-having revolt people-among having-made-mount, right? so? to-be-done became saying
sentences.i: ‘We, being of another mind (another “liver”), have set the people on horseback in revolt: is it right? is it so? — it has come to be done,’ saying (so),
sentences.n: This sentence is doubtful throughout. Ba is “we” (Ming 俺); helige-tü is “liver-having” (Ming 肝有的), busu helige a different heart; bulγa irgen-dür “among the people, in revolt” with morilaγ̇uldažu, “causing to mount”; žöbi, tabi (both Ming 是麽) are questions; bolqu bolba “it came to be done”. Who says this is not clear; I take it as part of what was said to Batu.

sentences.l: "Ene dörmegei ken-ü üġes-tür dölüsküžü aqa küġün-i aman düġüren ügülejü"
sentences.i: “This lowly fellow, egged on by whose words, speaks to his elder with his mouth full
sentences.n: Dörmegei here is the Ming's 下等 “low-grade”, an insult, not the place-name of earlier parts. Dölüsküžü is “egged on, joining the din” (Ming 趂閧着; stem inferred). Aman düġüren is “mouth full” (of words); compare the same phrase in the Qahan's later reproach. Shiratori closes the quotation after ügülejü; the speech plainly goes on, and is closed only at medetügei, so in the English I close it there.

sentences.i: Moṅγai, Alčidai, Qoṅγortai, Žaṅgi and the others: take the heart that has risen up, make it your companion at your side, and hold it back; for the boiling pot make a wide ladle, and let it be calmed.

sentences.t: "Buri-ji Čaγ̇adai aqa medetügei" keġebe.
sentences.l: "Buri-ji Čaγ̇adai aqa medetügei" keġebe.
sentences.i: ‘Let my elder brother Cha'adai deal with Büri,’ he said.
sentences.n: A second short order: Büri-ji is “Büri (object)”, with Cha'adai as the one to see to him. Büri was Cha'adai's kinsman and rival of Batu, so the matter goes to the elder prince; the Ming gives only “let him know” (知者).
